related_questions.question: Who is at risk for ascites?

text_blocks.snippet: Individuals with liver disease, particularly cirrhosis, are at the highest risk of developing ascites, which is the buildup of fluid in the abdomen. Other factors that increase risk include certain cancers, heart failure, kidney failure, and tuberculosis.
snippet_highlighted_words: Individuals with liver disease, particularly cirrhosis

list.title: Cirrhosis:
list.snippet: Cirrhosis, a condition where healthy liver tissue is replaced by scar tissue, is the most common cause of ascites.

list.title: Hepatitis:
list.snippet: Chronic hepatitis B and C infections can lead to cirrhosis and ascites.

list.title: Alcohol Abuse:
list.snippet: Excessive alcohol consumption over many years can cause severe liver damage and ascites.

list.title: Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis (MASH):
list.snippet: Previously known as non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), MASH can also lead to cirrhosis and ascites.

list.title: Heart Failure:
list.snippet: Heart conditions that impair the heart's ability to pump blood effectively can cause fluid buildup in the abdomen.

list.title: Kidney Failure:
list.snippet: Kidney disease can also lead to fluid retention and ascites.

list.title: Tuberculosis:
list.snippet: Tuberculosis, particularly when it affects the peritoneum, can cause fluid buildup.

list.title: Cancer:
list.snippet: Certain cancers, such as ovarian, pancreatic, liver, or endometrial cancer, can lead to ascites.

list.title: Pancreatitis:
list.snippet: Inflammation of the pancreas can also cause fluid to accumulate in the abdomen.
Obesity: Obesity is a risk factor for fatty liver disease and can indirectly contribute to ascites.
High Triglyceride Levels: High triglyceride levels can also be a risk factor.
Intestinal Bypass Surgery: This type of surgery can sometimes lead to complications that increase the risk of ascites.
Long-Term Corticosteroid Use: Prolonged use of corticosteroids can also be a risk factor.
